transcript.answer: No. Cross-family review is not a rule in Lore. ADR-039 ("Cross-model review for agent-authored changes") proposed it. It would have pinned the review agent to a different model family from the implementer, to counter self-preference bias. That ADR's status is still "draft", and its 2026-10-14 amendment withdrew the requirement. The amendment says `code-review` and `code-review-recheck` run on `gemini-4-argon`. That is the same family as the implementation loop's `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`. `code-review-reply` stays on `claude-sonnet-4-6`. The reason given is a local bench on five merged PRs with known must-fixes. Argon found all five that finished (one timed out) with no false alarms. Sonnet found four of six. Argon also caught a real bug that neither Sonnet nor the posted review caught (#2742). The ADR concluded that this catch rate outweighed the self-preference risk. It says "cross-family review is no longer a rule, only one input to the model choice." The cost is that Argon is about 3x slower and about 40% dearer per review. If same-family review starts to under-catch, the ADR says to rerun the same bench.

judgements.reason: The answer says no, that ADR-039 is a draft that only proposed cross-family review, and that the 2026-10-14 amendment put code-review and code-review-recheck on gemini-4-argon, the implementer's family, because it caught more, leaving cross-family as only one input to model choice.
